easy.name: Easy
easy.blurb: New to training or coming back after a break. Fewer moves, 2–3 sets and longer rests.

intermediate.name: Intermediate
intermediate.blurb: Some training experience. Compound lifts plus a finisher superset, 3 sets.

hard.name: Hard
hard.blurb: Trained regularly for a year or more. Harder variations, 4 sets and shorter rests.

goal.title: The goal, honestly
goal.fat-loss: Going from {{start}} kg to {{goal}} kg over {{days}} days is about {{rate}} kg a week.
goal.fatLossPaceOk: That's a safe pace you can keep up. The calorie deficit removes fat while protein and resistance training keep your muscle, so you end up leaner, not just lighter.
goal.fatLossPaceFast: That's faster than the 0.5–1 kg a week most people can sustain. Consider a later target date so you keep your muscle.
goal.muscle: Muscle builds slowly: about 0.25–0.5 kg a week at best. A small calorie surplus, enough protein and adding weight over time do the work.
goal.fitness: The goal is to get fitter and stronger. Eat at maintenance, train consistently, and let your logged sets show the progress.
goal.maintain: The goal is to keep your weight steady and stay strong. Eat at maintenance and keep showing up.
moves: Consistency beats intensity: get every planned session done, week after week.
Log your sets so the weights climb over time.
Eat about 1.8 g of protein per kg of body weight every day.
Walk 7,000–10,000 steps a day, especially on non-training days.
goal.homeKit: Everything here works at home with a pair of dumbbells and a resistance band. Tap any exercise for a demo in the gallery or a YouTube video.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.description: Every move links to its demo in the gallery and a YouTube video.

safety.title: Safety notes
knee: Knees track over toes, never caving inward.
Only move through a pain-free range. Shallow is fine, especially on wall sits and squats.
No bouncing or jumping anywhere in the plan.
Sharp pain means stop that move, take the swap, and keep going.
Warm up every session (the timer includes it).
If pain gets worse or lasts more than a couple of weeks, see a physiotherapist.
safety.disclaimer: FitPower is not medical advice. If you have a health condition, check with a doctor before starting.
